Summary: RECONX-E22 — Day 8: Vite setup, HOCs & compound DataTable
Description: Stand up the Vite + React 19 dev environment with path aliases, build withAuth and withErrorBoundary HOCs, and ship a compound <DataTable> whose sub-components share state via internal context. Groups TICKET-ADV111 through ADV114.

Summary: RECONX-E23 — Day 8: Custom hooks
Description: Build the four custom hooks the rest of the app leans on — useWebSocket, useTradeStream, useDebouncedSearch, and useInfiniteScroll — each with correct effect cleanup and dependency handling. Groups TICKET-ADV115 through ADV118.

Summary: RECONX-E24 — Day 8: Memoisation, code splitting, forms & theme
Description: Optimise the dashboard with React.memo, useMemo, and useCallback, add React.lazy + Suspense route-level code splitting, build a react-hook-form + yup trade entry form, and wire a persistent light/dark ThemeProvider. Groups TICKET-ADV119 through ADV124.

Summary: RECONX-E25 — Day 8: RTL tests & Profiler
Description: Close the day with React Testing Library coverage of the dashboard summary cards and a hands-on React DevTools Profiler session that measures and fixes unnecessary re-renders. Groups TICKET-ADV125 and ADV127.

Summary: TICKET-ADV111 — Vite setup with path aliases
Description: GOAL: configure the Vite project so @/components-style imports resolve everywhere, with no ../../.. relatives in the tree. DONE WHEN: npm run dev boots the Vite server on http://localhost:5173 within five seconds of a cold start. An import like import { StatCard } from '@components/StatCard' resolves at runtime and in the IDE (no red squiggles). At least five aliases are wired: @, @components, @hooks, @services, @context (plus @pages if present).

Summary: TICKET-ADV112 — HOC: withAuth(Component)
Description: GOAL: build a higher-order component that wraps any page and redirects unauthenticated users to /login before the wrapped component ever renders. DONE WHEN: export default withAuth(Dashboard) redirects to /login when no user is in AuthContext. The wrapped component is never visible — not even for a single frame — when logged out. React DevTools shows a useful display name (e.g. withAuth(Dashboard), not just WithAuth).

Summary: TICKET-ADV113 — HOC: withErrorBoundary(Component)
Description: GOAL: wrap any component in an ErrorBoundary that catches render errors and shows a recoverable fallback, exposed as an HOC so any page can opt in. DONE WHEN: throwing an error inside a wrapped component shows a fallback UI, not React's red screen. The fallback has a "Try again" affordance that resets the boundary's state and re-renders the children. A second error after reset is caught again (the boundary is reusable, not single-shot).

Summary: TICKET-ADV114 — Compound component: DataTable with Header, Body, Pagination
Description: GOAL: build a <DataTable> whose Header, Body, and Pagination sub-components share sort state and pagination via internal context, so callers compose them as children rather than flat props. DONE WHEN: DataTable.Header, DataTable.Body, and DataTable.Pagination work when nested inside <DataTable data>. Clicking a header cell sorts the body and toggles ascending/descending; pagination respects the current sort. Omitting <DataTable.Pagination /> still leaves a working table — sub-components are optional.

Summary: TICKET-ADV115 — useWebSocket(url, options) with exponential backoff
Description: GOAL: a custom hook that opens a WebSocket connection, exposes { data, status, send }, and reconnects with exponential backoff on unexpected close. DONE WHEN: mounting a consumer opens exactly one WebSocket and unmounting closes it (Network tab agrees). A forced server-side close triggers reconnects after growing delays (1s, 2s, 4s, ...) capped by a max delay and max retry count. send is a no-op when the socket isn't OPEN, and data updates on each parsed message.

Summary: TICKET-ADV116 — useTradeStream() with SSE
Description: GOAL: subscribe to the Day 7 server-sent events endpoint and return { trades, isConnected }, accumulating events into a bounded local buffer. DONE WHEN: mounting a consumer opens an EventSource against /stream/trades and unmounting closes it. New trades appear at the top of the returned array within ~1 second of backend emission. The buffer never exceeds a fixed cap (~200) — oldest entries fall off as new ones arrive.

Summary: TICKET-ADV117 — useDebouncedSearch(query, delay)
Description: GOAL: a hook that takes a raw query string and a delay, and returns a debounced version that only updates once typing has paused for delay ms. DONE WHEN: rapid keystrokes produce only one update to the debounced value after the user pauses. Changing the delay parameter at runtime changes the debounce window without leaking the old timer. Replacing every inline setTimeout/clearTimeout debounce with this hook produces the same behaviour.

Summary: TICKET-ADV118 — useInfiniteScroll(loadMore) with IntersectionObserver
Description: GOAL: a hook that returns a sentinelRef; attaching it to a sentinel element at the bottom of a list calls loadMore() whenever the sentinel scrolls into view. DONE WHEN: scrolling near the bottom triggers loadMore exactly once per intersection, not on every scroll event. loadMore callbacks are picked up on each render (no stale closures) while the observer is created once. Unmounting the consumer disconnects the observer — no memory leak across page navigations.

Summary: TICKET-ADV119 — React.memo on TradeRow with custom equality
Description: GOAL: wrap the trade row component in React.memo with a custom equality check so rows only re-render when fields they actually display change. DONE WHEN: updating unrelated dashboard state does not re-render existing trade rows (verified in the Profiler). Mutating a trade's status or price re-renders only that row. The equality function compares the precise fields the row reads (id, status, price, onClick identity) — no JSON.stringify shortcuts.

Summary: TICKET-ADV120 — useMemo for portfolio value and P&L aggregations
Description: GOAL: wrap genuinely expensive aggregations (portfolio value, matched/unmatched/disputed counts and totals) in useMemo so they recompute only when the trades array actually changes. DONE WHEN: re-renders triggered by non-trade state changes (e.g. opening a side panel) do not recompute the aggregations. A new trade arriving on the SSE stream recomputes them once. You can articulate why each memoised value is worth caching (cost vs cache overhead).

Summary: TICKET-ADV121 — useCallback on handlers passed to memoised children
Description: GOAL: wrap handlers passed into <TradeRow /> (and similar memo children) with useCallback so the memoisation from TICKET-ADV119 actually holds. DONE WHEN: the Profiler shows <TradeRow> only re-renders when its trade props change — not when the parent re-renders for unrelated reasons. Every useCallback dep array is honest: empty only when the closure needs nothing, otherwise listing every captured value. No useCallback exists for handlers never passed into a memoised child.

Summary: TICKET-ADV122 — React.lazy + Suspense route-based code splitting
Description: GOAL: lazily import each page component and place one <Suspense> boundary at the right level of the layout so first navigation downloads a per-page chunk and re-navigation hits the cache. DONE WHEN: the Network tab shows a per-route chunk-*.js downloading the first time a page is visited, and not on re-visits. A skeleton (not a spinner, not null) is shown while a chunk loads. The layout (nav, header) does not flash on navigation — only the page contents.

Summary: TICKET-ADV123 — Trade entry form with react-hook-form + Yup
Description: GOAL: build the /trades/new page as a react-hook-form form validated against a yup schema covering trade ref, instrument, quantity, price, and trade date. DONE WHEN: submitting a valid form sends a POST to /api/trades with parsed numbers (not string "1000"). Submitting an invalid form sends nothing; each field shows its specific error message with role="alert". The form does not re-render on every keystroke (RHF stays uncontrolled — verified in the Profiler).

Summary: TICKET-ADV124 — Theme context (light/dark) with persistence
Description: GOAL: provide a ThemeProvider exposing a useTheme() hook that persists the choice to localStorage, respects prefers-color-scheme on first visit, and flips data-theme on <html> so the existing CSS takes over. DONE WHEN: toggling theme flips a single attribute on the <html> element and the page restyles immediately — no JS-side colour values. Reloading the page preserves the chosen theme. First-time visitors with prefers-color-scheme: dark start in dark mode.

Summary: TICKET-ADV125 — RTL test: dashboard summary cards
Description: GOAL: render <Dashboard /> with seeded trade data inside the required providers and assert each summary card is present. DONE WHEN: npm run test (or vitest run) passes the dashboard test in isolation with no live backend. Queries use roles (getByRole('heading', { name: /portfolio value/i })) — not getByText and not getByTestId. A renderWithProviders(ui) helper wraps the UI in MemoryRouter, ThemeProvider, and AuthContext.Provider so the test does not crash on useNavigate/useTheme calls.

Summary: TICKET-ADV127 — Profile with React DevTools, fix unnecessary re-renders (fast-finisher)
Description: GOAL: open the React DevTools Profiler, record a session exposing excessive re-renders on the dashboard, identify the specific culprit, and apply a fix that reduces the render count in a follow-up recording. DONE WHEN: a before Profiler trace shows the bug (excessive render counts on a component that didn't need to update). You can articulate why the component rendered (which prop changed or which parent caused it). An after recording — same interactions, same data — shows materially fewer renders for the same component, and you can name the change that did it.
